# BlueTusk documentation

> PostgreSQL for .NET, with ADO.NET, EF Core, real-time data, graphs, and data services.

[Full documentation text](https://bluetusk.io/llms-full.txt)

## Getting started

- [Run your first query](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/quickstart): Run a parameterized PostgreSQL query from a new .NET console app.
- [Install BlueTusk](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/install): Choose packages and check what your PostgreSQL and .NET versions support.
- [Core concepts](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/concepts): Understand data sources, sessions, type identity, and committed changes.
- [BlueTusk documentation](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/handbook): Find the right documentation for the BlueTusk feature you use.
- [Architecture](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/architecture): See how the provider, EF Core, and change-delivery products fit together.
- [Explore complete examples](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/examples): Follow runnable samples and complete application workflows.
- [.NET, EF Core, and PostgreSQL compatibility](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/getting-started/runtime-compatibility): Match .NET 5–11, EF Core dependencies, and PostgreSQL features to your deployment.

## ADO.NET

- [ADO.NET](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/overview): Learn the ADO.NET API for connections, commands, readers, and transactions.
- [Dependency injection and health checks](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/dependency-injection): Register a shared data source and configure an application health check.
- [Authentication](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/authentication): Configure TLS, SCRAM, Kerberos, and client authentication.
- [Connection pooling](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/pooling): Size connection pools, manage leases, and control session reset.
- [Multi-host connections](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/multi-host): Connect to primary and replica hosts with explicit targeting.
- [Cloud identity](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/cloud-identity): Use cloud credentials and rotate database tokens.
- [Batches](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/batches): Send multiple parameterized statements in a batch.
- [COPY](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/copy): Bulk-import and export data with PostgreSQL COPY.
- [Large objects](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/large-objects): Read and write large objects inside transactions.
- [Asynchronous notifications](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/notifications): Listen for PostgreSQL notifications on a dedicated session.
- [Sequential readers](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/sequential-readers): Stream result values without buffering entire rows.
- [Schema discovery](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/schema-discovery): Inspect database and result-set metadata.
- [Use PostgreSQL types](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/types): Map PostgreSQL types, including domains, arrays, enums, composites, and ranges.
- [Core type mappings](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/types-reference): Look up type mappings and catalogue behavior.
- [PostgreSQL pipeline mode](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/pipeline-mode): Use pipeline mode within its transaction and cancellation boundaries.
- [Multiplexing compatibility](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/multiplexing-compatibility): Choose which commands can share a physical session.
- [NativeAOT and trimming](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/nativeaot): Prepare a trimmed or Native AOT .NET application.
- [Start PostgreSQL replication](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/replication): Read WAL and pgoutput changes through low-level replication APIs.
- [Replication](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/replication-reference): Configure replication sessions, messages, and LSN feedback.
- [PostgreSQL 19 native REPACK](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/repack): Run repack with the right PostgreSQL permissions and operational controls.
- [ADO.NET compatibility](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/provider/ado-net-compatibility): Check supported ADO.NET contracts and migrate provider-neutral code.

## EF Core

- [Use BlueTusk with Entity Framework Core](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/ef-core/overview): Configure a DbContext and use LINQ, migrations, and database scaffolding.
- [Entity Framework Core](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/ef-core/ef-core-reference): Look up type mappings, query translations, migrations, and provider configuration.

## Real-time data

- [BlueTusk real-time platform](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/platform): Choose Streams, Sync, Live, Continuous Graph, or Control Plane.
- [Delivery guarantees in plain language](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/contracts): Understand checkpoints, idempotency, replay, and delivery guarantees.
- [BlueTusk Streams](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams): Consume whole committed transactions from PostgreSQL.
- [Snapshot and catch-up](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/snapshot-bootstrap): Load existing rows and continue from the matching WAL position.
- [Streams checkpoint and lease stores](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/state-stores): Choose and configure durable checkpoint and spool storage.
- [Durable relay](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/durable-relay): Place durable storage between change capture and delivery.
- [Hosting and observability](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-hosting): Host the consumer and monitor slot lag, retries, and spool use.
- [Publish transactions as CloudEvents](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-cloudevents): Encode committed change deliveries as CloudEvents.
- [Prepared and two-phase transactions](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-prepared-transactions): Understand two-phase changes and settlement behavior.
- [Typed change mappings](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-typed-mappings): Decode change rows into generated or hand-written types.
- [Streams validation and provisioning CLI](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-cli): Inspect logical streams, run samples, and diagnose configuration.
- [Wire Streams into .NET Aspire](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-aspire): Configure Streams resources in a .NET Aspire host.
- [Run the snapshot-then-stream sample](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/streams-sample): Run a sample replication consumer and observe committed changes.
- [BlueTusk Sync](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/sync): Deliver change transactions to a destination with replay-safe identities.
- [BlueTusk Sync](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/sync-reference): Configure destination adapters, checkpoint behavior, and data mappings.
- [Push live updates to applications](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live): Register authorized, bounded queries and stream results to clients.
- [BlueTusk Live](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live-reference): Configure query plans, diffing, replay stores, transports, and browser clients.
- [Live format compatibility](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/live-format-compatibility): Understand versioned Live envelopes and replay store formats.
- [Keep graph query results current](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/continuous-graph): Keep an authorized graph result up to date after relevant commits.
- [BlueTusk Continuous Graph](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/continuous-graph-reference): Configure graph query plans, dependencies, maintenance, and replay.
- [Control Plane](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane): Manage registered database instances, pipelines, and operational resources.
- [BlueTusk Control Plane and Dashboard](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/control-plane-reference): Configure inventory providers, operations, permissions, and dashboard APIs.
- [Real-time operations](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/real-time/operations): Deploy and recover the real-time data pipeline.

## Graphs

- [Query a property graph](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/graph/property-graphs): Map vertex and edge tables and run typed, portable graph patterns.
- [BlueTusk Graphs reference](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/graph/graph-reference): Look up graph metadata, path semantics, migration options, and native SQL/PGQ.
- [Run a bounded traversal](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/graph/traversals): Run neighbors, reachability, and shortest-path queries with bounded work.
- [BlueTusk PostgreSQL graph engine](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/graph/engine): Install and operate the optional PostgreSQL server extension.

## Extensions

- [Use PostgreSQL extensions](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/extensions/catalog): Choose client integrations for PostgreSQL extensions and register their codecs.
- [Extension SDK](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/extensions/reference): Look up package names, supported types, and EF Core mappings.

## Data services

- [Choose a data service](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/overview): Choose a BlueTusk data service for your application.
- [BlueTusk.Documents](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/documents): Store JSONB documents, metadata, and streamed attachments.
- [BlueTusk.Events](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/events): Append ordered events and load application state by stream.
- [Published outbox retention: required protocol](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/event-retention): Manage event retention with registered consumers and safe watermarks.
- [BlueTusk.Projections](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/projections): Build queryable views of event streams with durable progress.
- [Explicit source recovery and controlled DDL](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/projection-recovery): Recover projections after reconnect, restart, or failover.
- [Published projections in Live](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/projection-live): Publish projection changes to authorized Live subscribers.
- [BlueTusk.Jobs](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/jobs): Enqueue, lease, retry, and complete durable background work.
- [Scoped Jobs and Workflows host readiness](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/jobs-hosting): Operate the job worker and configure leases and concurrency.
- [Durable storage maintenance contract](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/jobs-maintenance): Clean up completed jobs and maintain queue health.
- [Recover jobs after PostgreSQL failover](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/jobs-failover): Prepare for database failover and recover leased jobs.
- [Jobs and Workflows durable formats](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/jobs-durable-format): Understand the job database schema and durable data format.
- [Upgrade Jobs storage and workers](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/jobs-upgrade): Upgrade queues and workers without losing durable work.
- [BlueTusk.Workflows](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/workflows): Coordinate persistent steps and signals with explicit recovery policies.
- [BlueTusk Schema](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/schema): Compare PostgreSQL schemas and apply controlled schema changes.
- [Catalogue consistency attestation](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/schema-attestation): Check database catalogue state against an expected schema.
- [BlueTusk Sql](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/sql): Build and validate typed SQL catalogs.
- [BlueTusk.Search](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/search): Index data and query search or vector backends.
- [BlueTusk.Edge](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/edge): Synchronize client data through intermittent connections.
- [BlueTusk Studio](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/services/studio): Inspect PostgreSQL data through capability-authorized client queries.

## Operations

- [Production checklist](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/production-checklist): Review access, capacity, observability, recovery, and rollback before deployment.
- [Deployment and configuration](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/deployment): Deploy BlueTusk with PostgreSQL and configure its runtime dependencies.
- [Secure a BlueTusk application](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/security): Configure TLS, least privilege, tenant isolation, and safe telemetry.
- [Production observability and SLOs](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/observability): Instrument commands, pooling, logical replication, and real-time processing.
- [Troubleshooting](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/troubleshooting): Diagnose connection, query, type mapping, and change-delivery issues.
- [Performance engineering](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/performance): Measure and tune application workloads using realistic database access patterns.
- [Upgrade guide](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/upgrade-guide): Plan compatible upgrades across packages, PostgreSQL, and persisted state.
- [Diagnose deployment health](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/application-platform-health): Check application, worker, and database health.
- [Report a security issue](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/report-security): Report a suspected security vulnerability privately.
- [Use the BlueTusk command-line tools](https://bluetusk.io/documentation/operations/tools): Check a database connection, scaffold a model, or validate a typed SQL catalog.
